options: Creates a variable with a specified data type
questions.explain: DECLARE @VariableName DataType; is the syntax to create a variable.

questions.q: What must every T-SQL variable name start with?
questions.explain: The @ prefix distinguishes a variable from a column or table name at a glance.

options: Assigns a single value to a variable
questions.explain: SET @VariableName = value; assigns a value after DECLARE has created the variable.

questions.q: What is a common use of assigning a variable with SELECT instead of SET?
options: SELECT can only assign string values, never numbers
SELECT assignment is identical to DECLARE
SELECT cannot be used to assign variables in T-SQL
Capturing the result of a query (like an aggregate) into a variable for reuse later
questions.explain: SELECT @Var = AVG(ListPrice) FROM Product captures a computed value once, avoiding recalculating it multiple times.

questions.q: Can a variable be given an initial value directly in its DECLARE statement?
options: No, a separate SET statement is always required
Only when declaring multiple variables at once
questions.explain: DECLARE can include an initial assignment inline, as an alternative to a separate SET statement.
